entry.title: 🔴The Effects of Believing Life Is Meaningless✍️Mostafa Malekian1️⃣…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴The Effects of Believing Life Is Meaningless✍️Mostafa Malekian1️⃣ Boredom, Indifference, and a Vegetative LifeThe first effect of considering life meaningless is that life gradually takes on a vegetative state. A person no longer admires anything, has no deep interest in anything, and everything becomes monotonous and boring. Only when life is meaningful can a person praise something, become attached to something, and distinguish between different matters.In such a situation, life becomes the repetition of repetitions. Suppose someone is traveling from Tehran to Mashhad. Every time they stop at a gas station, they say: "I'm filling up the tank so I can reach Mashhad." This action has meaning because there is a destination.But if someone says: "I'm filling up the tank to reach the next gas station, and I'm going to the next gas station to fill up again and reach the next one," this cycle has no purpose and is mere repetition.Similarly, when life lacks meaning, a person's activities become aimless repetitions—just like a plant that bears fruit every year without knowing why.2️⃣ Nihilism, Anger, and FrustrationThe second consequence of considering life meaningless is nihilism. Nihilism means a person denies any meaning for life and even mocks those who attribute meaning to it.Moral psychologists believe such people typically suffer from:inner anger,a constant sense of frustration,and a kind of indifference toward the affairs of life.In their view, nothing truly matters; therefore, they don't feel much difference between various events and lose their sensitivity and attachment to life.3️⃣ Reduced Psychological Capacity to Cope with ProblemsThe third effect of considering life meaningless is the reduction of a person's psychological capacity. Meaning plays the same role for the mind and psyche that food plays for the body. Just as the body becomes weak if it doesn't receive food for several days, if life is meaningless for a person, their mind and psyche will also become weak and listless.As a result, a person finds less capacity to face life's problems and hardships. Enduring suffering means that after suffering befalls a person, they can tolerate and digest it within themselves. Coping with problems means having the strength to stand firm and resist before harm or injustice befalls them.According to moral psychologists, the meaningfulness of life strengthens both capacities in a person, but meaninglessness weakens both.@mostafamalekian

entry.title: 🔴The Effects of Meaningfulness in Life✍️Mostafa Malekian🔹According to…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴The Effects of Meaningfulness in Life✍️Mostafa Malekian🔹According to many moral psychologists, those who consider life meaningful experience at least three profound effects in their lives.1️⃣ Inner CoherenceThe first effect of a meaningful life is the creation of a kind of inner coherence. A person is usually composed of different domains: beliefs, feelings, emotions, desires, and will. These domains are not always in harmony with each other and sometimes conflict.That's why sometimes we do something and immediately blame, reproach, or condemn ourselves. It's as if one part of our being says: "Do this," and another part says: "Why did you do that?"This struggle shows that a person is at war with themselves and lacks inner peace. Moral psychologists believe that when a person considers life meaningful, a kind of harmony and compatibility emerges among the different domains of their being. The person is at peace with themselves and moves away from inner turmoil.2️⃣ Increased Capacity to Endure SufferingThe second effect of a meaningful life is an increased capacity to endure suffering. Life is nothing but a collection of events and relationships, and many of these events and relationships are painful and distressing. Someone who considers life meaningful can better endure these sufferings. The greater the capacity to endure, the less intense the suffering is felt. Sometimes the level of tolerance increases so much that what was previously considered suffering no longer carries the same weight.Therefore, the meaningfulness of life causes a person to develop greater capacity for facing life's pains and hardships.3️⃣ Giving Purpose to LifeThe third effect of a meaningful life is giving purpose to life. If a person considers life meaningful, they can better determine:* what they should pursue in life;* and what they should refrain from pursuing.Meaningfulness clarifies the direction of a person's movement and gives purpose to their life.@mostafamalekian

entry.title: 🔴 Why is having an ideology so attractive? What are the harms of ideological…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴 Why is having an ideology so attractive? What are the harms of ideological thinking?✍️Mostafa Malekian🔹Ideology means believing that for every question, there is only one answer; for every issue, only one solution; and for every problem, only one way to fix it. As if the truth has already been discovered and there is no longer any need to think, ask, or search.🔹But why are people drawn to ideology? Because the world is far more complex than we would like it to be. Life is full of ambiguity, doubt, contradiction, and uncertainty, and humans naturally suffer from such a state. They want to see the world as clear, orderly, and predictable.🔹Ideology precisely targets this need. It promises to clarify everything; to answer all questions, to have solutions for all problems, and to save people from confusion and ambiguity. That's why it has always been attractive to many people.🔹But this peace comes at a heavy price. The harms of ideology: The first cost is setting aside personal reason. When the answers to all questions are prepared in advance, you no longer need to think for yourself; someone else has thought on your behalf.🔹The second cost is losing personal responsibility. When someone else makes the decisions, the responsibility for those decisions is also lifted from your shoulders.🔹The third cost is the loss of freedom and free will. An ideological person no longer chooses; rather, they obey. Obedience replaces questioning, and "as you command" replaces "why?"🔹And finally, the most dangerous situation is when ideology falls into the hands of political power. In this case, those in power also present themselves as the owners of truth. They no longer merely govern people's behavior, but they determine what truth is, how the world should be seen, and what is right or wrong. From this point on, power not only dominates people's lives; it also claims ownership over truth.➖Part of the lecture introducing the book The Power of the Powerless@mostafamalekian

entry.title: 🔴What problems/questions exist regarding the statement "I…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴What problems/questions exist regarding the statement "I believe"?✍Mostafa Malekian1. What necessity is there for believing?Why should one believe? Is life somehow deficient without faith? Many people live good and happy lives without faith. Do we have a moral obligation to believe? Do we have a prudential obligation to believe?2. What does believing mean?Is believing an action or a passion? In believing, are we active or passive? That is, do I perform an act whose name is faith, or do I undergo a reception of an act whose name is faith?3. Is this faith above knowledge or below knowledge?When I believe, does it mean I am less than someone who knows, or more? That is, when I believe that "A is B," is this higher than the awareness and knowledge of someone who knows "A is B," or lower?4. Who determines the object of faith?Assuming that believing is necessary, what should I believe in? In what things? Should I believe in propositions or in beings? Should I say "I believe in God" or "I believe in the proposition 'God exists'"?5. What function does faith have in my life that makes me different from unbelief?That is, what distinctions do those who have faith in their lives have compared to those whose lives are without faith?➖Excerpt from a lecture at the unveiling session of the book Questions of Faith by Peter Berger@mostafamalekian

entry.title: 🔴Shariati was above all an orator✍Mostafa Malekian🔹 Shariati was, above…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴Shariati was above all an orator✍Mostafa Malekian🔹 Shariati was, above all, an orator. I mean he played with the feelings, emotions, and passions of his audience. But the intellectuals after the revolution are more teachers and instructors. Even in their lectures, they teach. When you listen to a lecture by Dr. Ali Shariati, you experience a surge of feelings, emotions, and passions. You say he's right, bravo, and hurrah... But when his lecture ends, if someone asks you what the essence of Dr. Shariati's lecture was, you'll find that, like a fish slipping from your grasp, you have nothing in your hand.🔹You can't say, for example, that the lecture had an introduction, three preliminary points, one thesis, and two arguments. Because he was an orator. He was from the region of Khorasan, and in that region we had masterful orators, like Fakhreddin Hejazi. "Much ado about nothing." God rest his soul, but whenever I think of him, I recall Shakespeare's saying, "Much ado about nothing." Shariati was an orator, and I mean that in the sense of Aristotle's five arts of rhetoric. That is, he dealt with emotions, feelings, and passions.🔹But when you sit and listen to the post-revolution intellectuals, your feelings, emotions, and passions are not engaged, and you constantly have to think about what his argument was. [...] When I say this is not a condemnation, I mean they are teachers. That is, they work with the audience's mind, they argue, they present theses, they critique the arguments of opponents, and they seek to strengthen their own reasons. Can you recall any lecture by Dr. Shariati where he says, "In this lecture, I have two theses? The first thesis is supported by one argument, and the second by three arguments." In all of Shariati's lectures, you cannot find a single instance like that.➖Part of a conversation between Ali Zamaniyan and Mostafa Malekian@mostafamalekian

🔴Mostafa Malekian:🔹If someone says that five years ago you used to say "A," so why don't you believe it anymore? I say: Yes. Five years ago, I sincerely and seriously believed in "A," but I no longer have any reason for that belief, and I owe no shame or apology to anyone, and I have no guilt either. As soon as I find a reason to change a belief, I change it, even if I've held it for thirty or forty years. If I now find a new belief that differs from my previous ones, I accept it with complete honesty and never allow my past or even my present to limit me.@mostafamalekian

entry.title: 🔴Why do people turn to superstition?✍️Mostafa Malekian🔹The meaning of…
entry.summary:
Source: @mostafamalekian

🔴Why do people turn to superstition?✍️Mostafa Malekian🔹The meaning of superstition, in the view of the Stoics, is that when there is a natural cause for something, we ignore that natural cause and consider an unnatural one instead.For example: Because I treated my wife so badly, we got divorced a year after our marriage.🔹Well, what is the natural cause? That you were ill-behaved; neither your words, nor your actions, nor your body language, nor your spending, nor your earning was right; well, you got divorced. That's called a natural cause.🔹But if you said: "On the night we were going to get married, the moon was in Scorpio, and that was the factor that caused our divorce," that becomes superstition.And here we must pay attention to the natural cause, not the unnatural ones (superstition).And we usually turn to superstition and unnatural causes because:1. We hide our own guilt.He says: "What could I do, man? It wasn't in my hands; the moon was in Scorpio!" I no longer say what behavior I engaged in, because I would become the guilty one.Or for example, he says: "I had left the broom upside down in the courtyard, and that was the reason my son and daughter-in-law had a fight!"Because we don't want to see what the real cause of our son and daughter-in-law's problems is, and to escape this responsibility and guilt, we turn to superstition.2. We don't seek to make amends.Because whenever we refer to natural causes, we must seek to make amends; but to avoid making amends and to escape responsibility for our mistakes, we turn to unnatural causes (superstition).➖Mostafa Malekian's lecture titled: Introducing the book "The Work of the Lighthearted"; Presenting 53 Teachings of the Stoic Epictetus@mostafamalekian
